nicole: Flagging a subtle teardown problem we hit in the Go quickstart workshop. Minimal repro below, leaving notes about ergonomics.

nicole: Repro summary: call Generator.Iter, read one token, cancel the caller ctx. Some internal goroutines (handshake / auth retry) don't observe cancel and the iterator doesn't close.

nicole: Minimal snippet: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, err := client.Generator(ctx, req)
if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
_ = iter.Next()
cancel()
// expect iter.Next/iter.Close to return; sometimes hangs
```

ben: Thanks. Is this observed only on Iter or also Streaming callback? In my tests Stream blocks on a chan send if consumer is slow, Iter hangs in handshake if auth retries are racing.

vlad: Two distinct roots we've seen before: (1) backpressure: SDK sending into a buffered channel without selecting on ctx.Done(); (2) background retry/auth goroutine using a derived ctx not wired to caller ctx. Both can prevent shutdown.

nicole: Exactly. Workshop sample app had a rate-limited consumer which exposed (1). Also using default auth refresher so (2) plausible.

ben: Short fixes: ensure every goroutine uses the provided ctx and channel sends use: `select { case out <- v: case <-ctx.Done(): return }`. That lets cancel unwind deterministically.

vlad: Agreed. DX/API follow-ups: Go SDK should give clear, idiomatic teardown primitives similar to Python/Node. Ideas: 
- Make iter implement io.ReadCloser semantics (Close returns quickly and is idempotent).
- Provide `iter.Stop()` (graceful) and `iter.ForceStop()` (immediate, may lose in-flight tokens).
- Offer GeneratorOption BackpressurePolicy: Block | BufferWithTimeout | DropOldest.

nicole: I like Close + ForceStop. Also add `CloseWithTimeout(ctx, dur)` to avoid callers having to roll their own goroutine hacks in examples. Quickstart currently says "call cancel" which is too vague.

ben: For consistency across SDKs, map: Python `aclose()` -> Go `Close()`; Node `.return()` -> Go `ForceStop()`. Add a short cross-language table in the DX docs.

vlad: Tests: add a unit that simulates slow consumer and asserts no goroutine leaks within 200ms after cancel across go1.20-1.22. Make it tolerant but catch obvious leaks.

nicole: I'll open a GH issue with repro + goroutine dump and add a tiny test. Also put a temporary note in the onboarding checklist recommending `BackpressurePolicy: BufferWithTimeout` for workshop exercises.

ben: Implementation plan: 1) patch auth refresher to accept the root ctx and ensure any spawned goroutine selects on ctx.Done(); 2) thread ctx into all channel sends; 3) add CloseWithTimeout and BackpressurePolicy as opt-in API (minor semver change).

vlad: UX nit: document semantics of ForceStop clearly ("may discard pending tokens and leave server-side partial state"). Also add a code snippet in quickstart demonstrating CloseWithTimeout so new users avoid leaks.

nicole: snippet for docs: 
```go
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer func(){ _ = iter.CloseWithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond) }()
for tok, ok := iter.Next(); ok; tok, ok = iter.Next() { /* handle */ }
```

ben: I'll take the auth refresher patch. vlad can own the API ergonomics RFC and docs. nicole please attach the goroutine dump and the minimal repro test to the issue.

devex-bot: Issue created: DEX-5342 "go generator teardown: ctx propagation + backpressure ergonomics" (assignee: ben) :white_check_mark:

nicole: thanks! adding a short note to the workshop guide so instructors mention BackpressurePolicy workarounds until we ship the fix. :thumbsup:
